headline: Australian security monitoring sector deeply underpenetrated and ripe for consolidation; Sydney is the 5th-largest per-capita CCTV market globally yet cameras are largely passive and unintelligent
reasoning: Hambling notes that large offshore security players — Fortune 300/500 enterprises — have neglected their Australasian operations, leaving the technology old and the industry fragmented. Sydney ranks 5th globally (outside China) for per-capita CCTV density, yet the cameras are not actively monitored or used to prevent crime. He sees a structural opportunity to modernise the industry by layering active AI-driven monitoring over existing camera infrastructure, and believes security is only becoming more important given current global conditions.
quote: And I remember walking the streets of Sydney and I had a bit of a moment where I looked up and realised there's cameras everywhere. And Sydney is the 5th largest per capita CCTV market in the world outside of China. But the cameras aren't doing anything. They don't do anything, they don't stop anything. They don't prevent anything. They just sit there looking. And then after an event, you know, if you're unfortunate enough to have one, you might be, might be able to download it and you might be able to take the police and you might be able to get some sort of insurance cover. And we had these monitoring rooms, very small and, and it was all about messy at the time and it well, wasn't anyone actually able to action these cameras, monitor them, use them.

headline: UK expansion managed conservatively — integrating culture first, not chasing short-term growth; stock is cheap, not on 20-30x earnings, and targeting ASX 100 scale over multi-year horizon
reasoning: Hambling says the UK acquisition (a former busted business) is being integrated culturally before any growth is pushed through, and investors should not over-expect near-term UK growth. He notes the share price is up 10x since he took over as MD and that EPS this year equals the share price at the time of his appointment. He explicitly flags the stock is cheap, not trading on 20-30x earnings, and says the company made deliberate trade-offs in the recent result that pushed toward the bottom of guidance in order to invest for two-to-three-year growth. The ambition is to become an ASX 100 company, and he is only seeking long-term, aligned institutional shareholders rather than short-term traders.
quote: Firstly, we're very cheap. So it's not like we're training on 20 or 30 times earnings. And secondly, you know, like we are here, we really only want, I'm really only, you know, interested in probably talking to people that want to see a great Australian industrial rise again, because that's what we're here to try to do. And once again, that question of trust with shareholders, how important is that board accountability and governance in your business?

headline: Record FY26 result driven by organic growth acceleration after M&A-led scale-building phase; only ~7% of Australian properties have security monitoring versus ~20% globally, representing a large runway
reasoning: Dennison Hambling explains that Intelligent Monitoring Group first used M&A to build the scale (technicians, control rooms, technology) needed to compete, and is now shifting to organic growth. The business is seeing around 7% organic growth in Australia. He highlights that only ~7% of Australian properties currently have security monitoring versus roughly 20% globally, and argues the industry has been old, fragmented and underloved by large offshore incumbents, creating a significant opportunity. The company's strategy is to deploy AI-enabled video monitoring — cameras that actively detect and deter events rather than passively record — across commercial and residential premises at scale.
quote: Now it's organic. So now we're we're very much put this business together as you would say, given again the history so that it can grow. And I think, you know, when we do talk about the results, the key feature of the results is the organic growth that's starting to come through in Australia, around 7% of properties now I'm talking commercial buildings, Sydney, you know, Harbour CBD through to houses all around Australia have some form of security monitoring. And it's a bit old and antiquated and doesn't isn't predictive, it isn't reactive, it's reactive, not predictive. So that is very low on a global basis, probably 20% of businesses would have an intrusion alarm. That is very low. And again, it represents because the industry's been old and unloved, the opportunity for us is significant to now take this mess where we've got the technology, where we're catching criminals every day with the police as they're an event or even stopping them from, you know, actually causing an event to take that right out around, you know, every premise.

headline: Record revenue and return to statutory profit driven by M&A scale, organic growth, UK acquisition and re-entry into commercial market serving top ASX-listed companies
reasoning: Intelligent Monitoring Group has delivered record revenue and returned to statutory profit, driven by M&A-led scale and increasing organic growth as more customers take higher-value services. The company split its ADT Pacific acquisition into separate Australia and New Zealand businesses and has re-entered the commercial market, now servicing approximately 35 of the top 50 ASX-listed companies with access control, cameras and monitoring. A UK acquisition was funded via debt at approximately 3x net debt/EBITDA, which management characterises as standard industrial gearing for a highly recurring revenue business (92% recurring in the UK asset). The UK business is the longest-standing security brand in that market with over 160,000 customers, and Johnson Controls took a stake via the deal. Management cautioned against over-expecting near-term UK growth, framing near-term focus on cultural integration rather than aggressive expansion.
quote: We've just recently bought the UK business too. We have in Australia and in New Zealand we've re entered the commercial market. So we now would be dealing with today I think the top 35 of the top 50 largest A6 listed companies providing them, you know this electronic security solution, so access control, cameras, monitoring all those things... The UK business we bought is very stable. It's 92% recurring revenue. So, you know, distinct to some of the corporate stories of Australia, we're not going and buying a commodity up and down hope business. We're buying an existing play, the longest standing security brand in the UK market with an existing customer base of over 160,000 customers who pay their bill every month.
